topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and outline the core learning objectives and themes of the lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a disruption of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These sections define cancer as a breakdown of normal developmental differentiation and tissue structure driven by accumulated genetic changes, while considering the limitations of in vitro models.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and stepwise progression
topics.groupedBecause: These sections explain how tumors invade surrounding stroma and disseminate metastatically, using histological specimens and colorectal cancer to illustrate the stepwise transition from benign to malignant states.

topics.label: Clinical risks, nomenclature, and mechanisms of tumor morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These sections examine how benign and malignant tumors are systematically classified and how their localized and systemic actions cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These sections review the frequency and mortality of major tumor types in humans and compare cancer occurrence across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These sections assess the clinical presentation of cancer and evaluate the efficacy and practical challenges of screening programs for different organ sites.

topics.label: Closing housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding remarks summarize the session's learning outcomes and provide logistical information for upcoming practicals and lectures.
